findings.evidence: `rg -n "dixonH2_norm_le|hM" code/TauCeti/Analysis/Contour` shows only `DixonH2Bound.lean:55:theorem dixonH2_norm_le ... (hg : IntervalIntegrable ...)` and no remaining `hM` wrapper.
findings.fix: Keep the L¹ theorem under a new name or add a compatibility theorem with the old uniform-bound statement/name deriving `≤ M / (‖w‖ - R) * |b - a|`.
findings.issue: `dixonH2_norm_le`'s public signature was changed from the uniform `M` bound to an `IntervalIntegrable`/L¹ bound, so existing users with only `hM : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, ‖f (γ t) * deriv γ t‖ ≤ M` lose the old theorem and cannot call the new one without separately proving integrability.

findings.evidence: `rg -n "dixonH2_tendsto_zero|hM" code/TauCeti/Analysis/Contour` shows only `DixonH2Bound.lean:66:theorem dixonH2_tendsto_zero ... (hg : IntervalIntegrable ...)` and no uniform-bound variant.
findings.fix: Retain the old `hM`-based tendsto theorem as a corollary, or rename the new L¹ version and keep the old name for compatibility.
findings.issue: `dixonH2_tendsto_zero` likewise drops the exported uniform-bound form and now requires `IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ f (γ t) * deriv γ t)`, breaking callers of the old public decay-at-infinity theorem.

summary: The new L¹ decay API is useful, but this PR removes the previously exported uniform-bound entry points instead of preserving them as compatibility corollaries.
